title: Date parts: ISO weeks, weekday 1–7, floor before 1970
verdict: ISO week and year; Monday is 1; parts and epoch floor
description: `week` is the ISO week and `iso_year` its year (2024-12-30 is week 1 of 2025; 2021-01-03 is week 53 of 2020); `weekday` runs from Monday 1 to Sunday 7; `millisecond` and `microsecond` are the fraction of the second in those units.

Before 1970 parts floor: 1969-12-31 23:59:59.5 has `second` 59, `microsecond` 500000, `epoch('s')` -1, and `truncate('1s')` goes down to 23:59:59. `truncate('1w')` goes to Monday, `'1mo'`, `'1q'`, `'1y'` to the first day.
reference: `date_part` and `date_trunc` (`Time.lean`): ISO weeks, Monday-based `isodow`, flooring before the epoch; their range is open in the reference.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
